newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS WEEK SOFTER ON UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS WEEK SOFTER ON UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was trading softer on most hard currencies on Monday morning but foreign exchange dealers expected a generally quiet day with little movement on the rates.
"The market is very quiet at the moment, there's nothing on the cards yet," one dealer said.
"Indications are that there could be some tobacco sellers in the market but not enough I think to move it. The money is likely to be swallowed up by imports," he added.
At around 0810 GMT the local unit was quoted at 11.3775/3875 on the U.S. dollar from 11.3750/3850 and was at 19.0850/1130 from Friday's 19.0240/0500 versus sterling.
Against the mark it eased to 6.3510/3560 from 6.3240/3300 but was quoted firmer on the rand at 2.4875/4885 compared to 2.4940/5000.
